title: Quarantine the battery cell that was dropped, charge the other three
instruction: One of the four battery cells was dropped. Put it in the red quarantine bin and the other three in the charger.
context: A dropped lithium cell can be damaged internally and must not be charged; after it is put back it looks exactly like the others. The robot must remember which cell fell.
setup: On a wooden bench in front of two arms mounted 61 cm apart: a grey plastic holder (fixed) 13 cm in front of the arm bases on the centre line with four square pockets (6.5 cm, 2.5 cm deep) at 6 cm and 15 cm left and right of the centre line, each holding an identical blue plastic dummy cell (3.4 cm diameter, 7 cm tall, 100 g); a black charger (fixed) 21 cm out with three pockets of the same kind at the centre line and 7.5 cm left and right; a red open quarantine bin (10 x 10 cm, 6 cm walls) 30 cm out on the centre line. During the first 6 s, while the arms are held still, the operator lifts one cell (cycles through the four) to 30 cm above the bench at 30 cm out and 20 cm left (1 s to 2 s), lets it fall, and at 3.5 s picks it up from where it landed and stands it back in its own pocket (by 5 s). The robot is commanded from 6 s.
scoring: 0.25 per good cell standing upright and still in a charger pocket (centre within 2 cm, bottom within 1 cm of the pocket floor); 0.25 for the dropped cell resting inside the bin (centre over the bin floor, bottom within 3 cm of it); success (1.0) when all four hold for 1 s. The score is set to 0 if the dropped cell is set down in a charger pocket. The episode ends with the score so far if a good cell is set down in the bin or a cell falls off the bench.
run_limit: 1600 steps (80 seconds at 20 Hz), including the 6 s observation phase during which actions are ignored
reset_notes: Stand the four cells in the holder, empty the charger and bin; pick the next cell to drop and perform the lift, drop and return as described (dummy cells, no electrical hazard).
fidelity: Approximate: the fall is simulated by physics from a scripted release; the cell is returned upright by a scripted move from its landing spot; no damage model.
